original_card.question: Can one selected pricing or assembly claim be checked by a genuinely independent exact implementation?
methods: Reconstruct the rank ledger from original operations rather than trusting its aggregate.
Implement certified moment inequalities through a different exact enclosure method.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Demonstrate independence, source binding, positive cases and semantic failure controls.

first_step.inspect: Record the selected certificate and complex_profile rather than taking a PR headline as input.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Recompute one small part of the ledger or one certified enclosure using an independent implementation.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Independent pricing prevents unsupported frontier claims and can reveal genuine accounting slack.
allowed_variations: Reconstruct either a source ledger or a numeric enclosure with a different method.
scope_change_triggers: Importing the primary function and calling its output independent verification.

actual_scope: Rebuild the selected frontier1094 complex rank ledger (and, unchanged, the frontier1042 checkpoint and two T8 ancestors) from the emitted hosted GLOBAL-TEMPLATE and the dispatched LOCAL-PROGRAMS, CANONICAL-WORD and DATA-PHASES that the certificate binds, by code-disjoint standard-library code, and require it to equal the certificate's complex_profile.
scope_change_reason: The card's ledger method applied to the one link that INDEPENDENT1094 and #1091/#1209 leave to author code: the emitted program versus the priced aggregate. That link is the 'exact exhaustive recursive-child profile' premise (research/native-complex-moment552/PROOF.md) behind the surcharge-free native complex recurrence of the selected kappa. The moment-enclosure method is not repeated (already triply covered for this record).
bottleneck_link: The surcharge-free complex recurrence of the selected kappa rests on two premises of the PR552/PR559 review: (a) an exact exhaustive recursive-child profile (PROOF.md lines 17, 24) and (b) no good/bad q-adic selector (lines 9, 24). This package checks, at source level, that the priced aggregate equals the emitted recursive children of the program the certificate binds, which is part of (a). It does not address (b), the classification rule or the hosting semantics, and it does not change kappa.
stop_rule: Stop when the rebuilt ledger equals the certificate for the selected record and the unchanged code reproduces the frontier1042 checkpoint, with every semantic and packaging control rejected by its named check; or stop and report a mismatch with its first failing check.
evidence: RESULT.json: frontier1094 ledger {1:349604, 2:60192, 3:62585, 4:20448, 5:11808, 7:7, 8:1152, 48:4866} rebuilt from 144 calls dispatched by 144 bound local sweeps (80 forward, 64 backward; per call {1:2412, 2:418, 3:432, 4:142, 5:82, 8:8} by a code-disjoint frame replay) plus 7526 emitted remainders {1:2276, 3:377, 7:7, 48:4866}; every owner-map slot executed by exactly one call route; all 14336 families carry 72 units; mass 1041408, D = 5120; equals ASSEMBLY, OWNERS-AND-PROFILE and INDEPENDENT1094. The frontier1042 checkpoint and two in-capsule T8 ancestor assemblies pass unchanged. test_package.py: 43 tests (36 semantic controls including consistent forgeries found by a post-PR soundness review, 6 packaging controls, positives).
author: Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar)
ai_assistance: Substantial: Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code. Parallel read-only scout and judge subagents selected and designed the check; two adversarial judges and a live Discussions sweep found the overlaps documented in README.md.

open_questions.blocked_by: No maintainer replay capsule for those claims on main yet.
